overview: Activity on November 17-18 featured three notable multi-patch series touching core BPF infrastructure. Mike Bazov submitted a v3 series to fix preemption safety in tracing programs by tracking recursion per task rather than per CPU, and Ihor Solodrai introduced kernel-side kfunc flavor support in libbpf to allow disambiguation when kfuncs share a family name. Shihuang Liu contributed two separate verifier and map-validation patches targeting variable-offset special-field checks and offloaded map restrictions.

patches.title: bpf: Check recursion per task for preemptible programs
patches.author: Mike Bazov
patches.summary: This v3 series addresses a correctness issue with preemptible BPF tracing programs that share per-CPU private stacks: when such a program is preempted and re-entered on the same CPU, the stack can be corrupted. The fix avoids using per-CPU private stacks for preemptible programs and instead introduces per-task recursion tracking via bpf_ctx, so that only one instance of a preemptible program runs per task at a time. A new flag marks programs whose runs must not overlap on a CPU, and selftests exercise the new recursion enforcement path.

patches.title: libbpf: Support kernel-side kfunc flavors
patches.author: Ihor Solodrai
patches.summary: Kfuncs can now have kernel-side "flavors" (variants with a ___ suffix) that adjust their prototype for different calling contexts. This series teaches libbpf to fall back to those kernel-defined ___ flavors when it cannot resolve a kfunc directly, and updates resolve_btfids to reject kfunc families that libbpf would be unable to disambiguate. Documentation describing how to change a kfunc's prototype is added alongside the selftests.

patches.title: bpf: Check variable-offset accesses against special fields
patches.author: Shihuang Liu
patches.summary: The BPF verifier previously did not validate variable-offset memory accesses against special fields such as spin locks, timers, and RB-tree nodes embedded in map values. This v4 patch closes that gap by running the special-field access checks during variable-offset range analysis, preventing programs from inadvertently aliasing or corrupting these kernel-managed fields through dynamic pointer arithmetic.

patches.title: bpf: Reject offloaded maps as map-in-map inner maps
patches.author: Shihuang Liu
patches.summary: This two-patch v2 series adds two validation checks to prevent misuse of map types that cannot serve as valid map-in-map inner maps. The first patch rejects offloaded maps (hardware-offloaded via XDP) from being used as inner maps, and the second rejects any map lacking iter_seq_info from being passed to bpf_iter_attach_map. Both fixes address paths where the kernel would otherwise proceed with an unsupported configuration.

patches.title: libbpf: Zero-extend unsigned 32-bit enum values in CO-RE relocations
patches.author: Yonghong Song
patches.summary: CO-RE relocations for 32-bit enums were sign-extended rather than zero-extended when the enum was declared unsigned, causing incorrect runtime values on little-endian hosts when the high bit of the 32-bit value was set. This two-patch series fixes libbpf to zero-extend such values during relocation and adds a selftest that exercises unsigned 32-bit enum CO-RE relocations to prevent regression.

patches.title: rqspinlock: Keep claiming the lock while the queue head is still the tail
patches.author: Shashank Mohan Jain
patches.summary: The resilient queued spinlock (rqspinlock) implementation had a subtle livelock risk: once a CPU became the queue head, it would stop trying to claim the lock if the tail had not yet advanced, forcing an unnecessary wait. This v2 patch keeps the head CPU claiming the lock as long as it is simultaneously the tail, eliminating the needless stall and improving throughput under low-contention workloads.
